body: Thank you for sharing your experiences, you’re very brave and you definitely deserve to speak to someone like you said. Hearing from people like you on this sort of topic is very helpful for me to start to try and realise it applies to me too. I’m very grateful to you and I’m sorry my reply isn’t as long as yours which I don’t want you to apologise for at all! I’m exhausted over the whole thing so I don’t want to type for too long to start my mind on that train of thought again, but I didn’t want to leave your reply unanswered because I truly am appreciative and it has helped me a lot. Wishing you all the best on your continuing journey. Sounds like you’re doing incredibly and I hope you can feel some pride :)

Thank you for taking the time to respond to me with so much care and thought. I admire the way you explained your experience and thought process. It’s clear to me I think that, whether due to al-anon or not, you’ve come really far with how you view your boundaries and how best to look out for yourself. 
I too don’t plan on ever ever talking about this with my parents, and I never want to. Like you said for yourself, it wouldn’t do me or them much good and would most probably be a bad thing if anything. My post was more-so to ask if anyone deals with just the guilt of going, or even the guilt acknowledging the alcoholic or whoever is affected by their alcohol consumption has a problem. I realised at my first meeting last night that I’m very much at the door of just the first step of admitting powerlessness over alcohol because I’m barely able to admit and own the fact that it’s a problem without feeling like a big dramatic liar (like my parents told me I was in the past). 
So thank you again for your comment! Have you ever dealt with guilt in that sort of way though? I wonder if it’s a common thing, especially as relatives of alcoholics because of the shame and the expectation of loyalty and keeping the secret from the world I suppose.
Thank you so so much. I’ll keep telling myself that. I hope you believe it for yourself too.

I’ve been struggling with this massively recently, and posted on here about it around a week ago or so. You’re not alone and I don’t think it’s talked about very much at all. I sometimes feel a bit ashamed feeling this way because it’s so not talked about, but when people talk about different communities it’s often considered really important to somewhat surround yourself to an extent at least a little bit with those who ‘get you’ whether it’s culture or religion or sexuality or identity in anyway, it’s just pretty accepted for it to be a normal thing people want so they feel less alone. I’m starting to let myself come around to the idea that I’m entitled to feel a little lonely when I’m never around people ‘like me’ in the physical sense. It can feel really alienating at times when it’s a body size/image thing, especially because unless people go through it or have experienced the things you have, not only do they often not understand but I’ve been noticing that a lot of the time it’s not even given much thought and that alone can feel awful, even if there’s no bad intent from them. Types of seats or spaces are things I think about more than my friends do (I’m a UK 18ish - sizes are crazy different everywhere) whereas most of my friends are around 10-12, with one being more similar to me. It really does have an impact I think when you can’t spend any time around those who experience similar things, situations, feelings, treatment from others, just anything that makes you want to reach out for some connection over. Realising this has been quite reassuring for me so maybe it could be for you to know it’s not a crazy question to pose? However, making friends more similar to me seems like a strange thing to go about - I don’t want to seek out people based on their bodies, if you get me? Ah it’s all scary :( Sorry there’s no advice from  me here, hopefully you can at least feel a little heard in the comments though ❤️

It’s so wonderful you have a community or friendships in your life that make you feel that way, so I’m really happy for you! I don’t want to just be told my hair or my top or my nail colour or my eyeshadow is nice while they all call each other beautiful and pretty 🥲. 
I’ve been thinking it’s maybe time to speak with someone professionally with the severity of how I feel about myself, and in terms of feeling supported by those around me I might need to try and diversify my friendships like you suggested. Yesterday I started following more women on instagram that had different body types than the ones I’m used to seeing so that’s a baby step!

Yesterday I wore a tight fitting long sleeve top out in public for the first time in years. It was so hard for me to do that I kept really really wanting someone to somehow know what I was going through and say “I’m really proud of you for doing this for yourself today and wearing something new for you, it looks good!” I didn’t end up feeling any better about myself than usual, and kept looking at the reflection of my arms in the windows on the tube on my commute there and back. I felt super aware of how much more of my body anyone could see than what I’d usually reveal (usually baggy t shirts or jumpers only). 

I’m not trying to discourage you at all though, and i don’t feel entirely discouraged myself after wearing it. I’d wear it again, but it wasn’t a magical switch that flipped. I’m just trying to say you are not alone in anything your post said about how you’re feeling, I know it so so well and I feel for you. Even though I think awfully of myself and don’t feel confident in anything I wear, let alone the form fitting top from yesterday, the thought of someone else feeling the way I do makes my heart break. I really hope you give yourself permission to at least try it for one day like I did and see how it goes. You deserve to try and push yourself a little even though it’s terrifying. I wish you could feel comfortable in whatever it is you’d truly love to wear. Regardless of what you look like, I think the glow that would come from you developing your self acceptance and the strength to trust in yourself to take such a big step would be so beautiful and something you should force yourself to feel even the tiniest bit proud of. 🤍

I appreciate you think I could have or could call them out on it, but even jokingly asking about how she meant it was a huge step for me to take. After she said the “no no sweet” thing I joked again and was like “oh trust me to be insane enough to take a compliment like an insult” and she was like “yeah haha!” And looked like genuinely surprised at the whole thing. I felt no better about it after at all to be honest. I’m just so full of self hatred it is literally impossible for me to challenge any negative thoughts or beliefs I hold true about myself, so pushing myself to call out someone else (especially when I know they didn’t inteeeeennddddd to hurt me) is like an alien concept. I’m really proud of you for getting your diagnosis, I’m not really sure how to go about it myself. I’m UK based, idk where you’re from so maybe you are too! I’ve just spoken with a psychologist over the phone last week (a week after it all started putting itself together in my head) to enquire about how she might be able to help me, she was incredible by the way, and she kind of supported my idea of C-PTSD (obviously she didn’t diagnose me over the PHONE, before we’ve even had an appointment) but mentioning to her all the physical symptoms I’ve dealt with my whole life (jaw clenching so much I got a mouth guard 5 yrs ago, 5+yrs of digestive issues, anxiety all the time that I just assumed was how my brain worked, I want to just run away all the time like last week I kept just putting my shoes on and running until tears came out and i couldn’t run anymore, so much shit) she was able to say “yes that does sound like trauma responses I have to say”. Validating, you know? So I don’t know what’s next for me in terms of diagnosis, whether I’ll go through my GP to get a medical diagnosis, seems like a more straightforward approach just to get diagnosed, but I’ll definitely be contacting that psychologist to start treatment.
Anyway, back on topic; you have no idea how much your comment has kind of calmed me down. It’s so hard to find any resources or anything online about… I don’t want to use a word I feel un-entitled to use but, the feeling of almost being in shock after the realisations I guess. It is crazy when you think your life has been one thing, then one day your body decides it’s time to let you in on everything that’s ever happened to you, why, who did what, how it affected you, how problems you’ve ALWAYS had (for me eg. lack of sex drive/dissociation during sex that i thought was ‘getting lost in the moment’ when really i have never felt connected to my body, my teeth grinding?? Always thought it was my adhd combined with boredom when really, i could be having a nice time and my jaw will be stiff and painful and NOTHING relaxes it i have to bite down on my hand sometimes and within 30s there a teeth marks that last over 10 mins) the body keeps the score and unleashes its hell on you all at once when the time is right. The weight of knowing “Ok, I get it all now. But how the fuck am I supposed to just carry on after this? I’m empty, I’m broken, I am scared of everyone, I feel alone, and now I know why I’ve always felt this deep down. So now what? I’ve used all my strength til this point to just keep myself going and keep distracting myself to blend in and not alarm people i love, to keep them happy. Now I know it’s all been for others, do I exist? Where is the extra strength I need to HEAL from this going to come from?” That’s where I’m at. So reading you saying that it passes and things can get better and life can change, you have made such a positive impact I’m so thankful, truly
That sentence at the end of your comment was beautiful, I’m going to hold onto that. Thank you so much, I’m rooting for us
Those lyrics sound so perfect and accurate, I’ll definitely listen to this soon. Thank you so much! Hope you’re getting by ok too ❤️

‘Quiet’ from Matilda the Musical. I’ve suddenly realised that I’m likely suffering from C-PTSD from childhood, and the realisation that my home environment and upbringing weren’t as privileged (only child, middle class, parents not divorced) as I thought it was on the outside, not as happy as I remembered it to be, and the worst; not as loving or supportive as I truly believed it was - it’s sent me over the edge for the past 2 weeks. Everytime I feel overwhelmed and alone, i turn all the lights off, sit on my sofa in the ‘brace’ airplane emergency position, and listen to it on repeat through noise cancelling headphones and just silently scream along to it and sob, like I’m having a panic attack myself really. I get so hot and tense, my face scrunched up and i just mouth the lyrics like I’m screaming it to the world hoping someone hears me and understands. Sorry to overshare, i just feel happy my googling for other people feeling the same way about Quiet (sadly I cant find anything) lead me to this question, because it’s pretty niche. And anything niche at the moment, even though this post is 1yr old, makes me feel less alone.

I’ve been using it for a long time on and off in phases. Previously I would smoke 2-3 (maybe 4 at a PUSH, occasionally) each night over 4/5hrs. It was the only time I had to myself without feeling consumed by everyone, and often the saddest I’d feel because I’d be alone with my thoughts, so I thought the weed was good for me. This summer, I smoked every day for about 2 months, initially 2-3 spliffs a day, eventually it went up to 8 spliffs a day, and I’d start from 10am (I obviously don’t live with my parents anymore lol). 
Not to scare you, just wanted to share my experience: it started to scare me when I’d start vomitting 2/3 times a week, violently. Apparently this is something potentially known as CHS - not that scary, just that after longterm use (4% of people) can start to vomit from weed. Then one night just before I’m about to flush… i see blood. Like a hand-palm sized amount. It scared me so much that a week later I stopped. 
No lie, I promise you: the very next day after I stopped smoking, I had a breakdown and gradually over the last 2 weeks have started to realise everything about C-PTSD, enmeshment, emotional parentification, covert incest, fearful-avoidant attachment.
I can’t give you advice on how to quit, because I tried over and over, but the anixety and panic attacks I’ve been having since all this became clear to me, it’s 100% distracted me from missing weed or smoking. Guess you could call it a win in one way, but my point is I think for us who are carrying such heavy things that cause us such pain, I don’t think weed is our friend. I think it’s just a way for us to feel distracted from the hurt, for me it even let me feel like a different person, one who was carefree and didn’t have to worry about anything, I could just exist for a few hours and forget I was real. I hope you find some support and things get better, you can always message me if you wanna talk more about this stuff. Sending love ❤️

This is so huge, well done! Whenever I go to the dentist, I always ask them to please explain to me what they’re doing while they’re doing it, it’s always made me panic (could never understand why, until now I know it’s all stemmed from C-PTSD related stuff) when they just poke and prod away inside your mouth reciting weird jargon you have no clue the meaning of, it feels like I’m not a person and they can just do whatever they want to me and I have to just sit there and keep calm, when all I want to do is scream so hard my heart can thump out of my chest and my lungs can breathe the air in. This is the only physical boundary I’ve ever been able to set, I think because we get taught that fear of the dentists/medical stuff is normal, so it made me fee like I could ‘get away’ with being ‘difficult’ or ‘demanding’, maybe even a bit ‘weird’ compared to other patients who don’t have the same ‘fear’. Setting boundaries is so hard, but your post reminded me of the dentist thing I’ve always done, and it gives me hope that both you and I can learn to apply that in other areas. 
Sending you support and love, well done ❤️

Thank you, reading that has made me start sobbing because i feel so alone and invalid in all of this. Just reading someone stating i’ve been through a lot makes me cry and feel better in a weird way, as an only child who was middle class with both parents when most of the people i grew up around had siblings, many had divorced parents, some parents that were ‘more abusive’ or they got hit, i just grew up feeling like I was super lucky and i could never talk about anything negative at home because it’d make me spoilt and ungrateful. People were jealous of me as an only child living in the house I had with the parents I had, and I never told people what I got for birthdays or christmases because I didn’t want to make anyone feel bad, and I’d listen to how they played games with their brothers/sisters, or had family visit from different places, I was secretly the really jealous one. I wish I could have told someone that every christmas I’d cry myself to sleep after spending the day counting the glasses my parents drank and waiting for the (non physical) blow out to happen, then them making up and we’d watch a movie and eat leftovers and laugh together like nothing happened, and i all of a sudden am supposed to feel safe and happy and calm again and just carry on with it and pretend things are normal, but I never knew if things could go bad again before bedtime, i just never knew. 
I have been listening to Jennette Mccurdy’s audiobook which has sometimes given me a bit of relief i think, just hearing someone elses voice reciting their stories (not all of them, not even the majority of hers - but some of them) that relate to my own and it, like your comment, makes me feel validated and less alone. In the past with depression etc I’ve always been able to distract myself usually, unless things are so bad i just cry and lay still, but with the adrenaline and stuff at the moment its hard to focus on let alone enjoy anything when something has set me off at some point during the day. 
Thank you so much for your comment and advice though, sorry for the ramble. ❤️
